content.text:
I migrated `src/module.ts` to es-toolkit and wrote the result to `out/module.ts`. The exported signatures are unchanged. Type checking passes with `--strict --skipLibCheck`. Without `--skipLibCheck`, tsc reports two errors in es-toolkit's own `defer.d.mts` and `deferAsync.d.mts`. They come from my ad-hoc tsc flags, since `Disposable` isn't in the es2022 lib. I did not run the project's own type check or compare outputs against the original.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 636 bytes (min+gzip) and 95 bytes of own code. I did not measure the original, because lodash isn't installed. I tried other import paths, and this combination was the smallest:

- **`doubled`:** uses `mapValues` from `es-toolkit`.
- **`byNameKey`:** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`. It takes a key function rather than a property name, so there is a small adapter: `(row) => row.name`. Later rows with the same name still overwrite earlier ones.
- **`isBlank`:** uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The plain `es-toolkit` build has no `isEmpty` that handles numbers, booleans and null the way lodash does, so I used the compat version. Importing `mapValues` and `keyBy` from compat as well raised the size to 3405 bytes, so those two come from the main entry.

No lodash import remains.
